'''Ulrike Luise Tillmann''' [[Royal Society|FRS]] is a mathematician specializing in [[algebraic topology]], who has made important contributions to the study of the [[moduli space]] of [[algebraic curves]]. She was the president of the [[London Mathematical Society]] in the period 2021–2022.

She is titular Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Oxford]] and a Fellow of [[Merton College, Oxford]].<ref name="cv">{{citation | author=Ulrike Tillmann | title=Curriculum Vitae | year=2008 | url=http://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/~tillmann/cv.pdf | access-date=16 December 2008 }}.</ref><ref name="ww">{{cite web | url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/telegraph/multimedia/archive/01123/Who_s_Who_new_name_1123303a.pdf | title = Who's Who 2009: New Names | publisher = [[The Daily Telegraph]] | access-date = 17 June 2009 }}</ref> In 2021 she was appointed Director of the [[Isaac Newton Institute]] at the [[University of Cambridge]], and N.M. Rothschild & Sons Professor of Mathematical Sciences at Cambridge, but continued to hold a part-time position at Oxford.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/38254|title=Ulrike Tillmann appointed Director of the Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Sciences|publisher=University of Oxford Mathematical Institute|date=4 February 2021}}</ref>

== Education ==
Tillmann completed her ''[[Abitur]]'' at {{ill|Gymnasium Georgianum (Vreden)|lt=Gymnasium Georgianum|de|Gymnasium Georgianum (Vreden)}} in [[Vreden]].<ref name="cv" /> She received a [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] from [[Brandeis University]] in 1985, followed by a [[Master of Arts|MA]] from [[Stanford University]] in 1987. She read for a PhD under the supervision of [[Ralph Louis Cohen|Ralph Cohen]] at [[Stanford University]], where she was awarded her doctorate in 1990.<ref name="cv" /><ref name=mathgene>{{MathGenealogy|id=39171}}</ref> She was awarded [[Habilitation]] in 1996 from the [[University of Bonn]].<ref name="ww" />

== Awards and honours ==
In 2004 she was awarded the [[Whitehead Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation | author=The London Mathematical Society | title=Annual Report 2004 | year=2004 | url=http://www.lms.ac.uk/policy/annualreports/report04.pdf | access-date=16 December 2008 | archive-date=8 January 2007 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070108123755/http://www.lms.ac.uk/policy/annualreports/report04.pdf | url-status=dead }}.</ref>

She was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society in 2008<ref>{{cite web|title=Fellows of the Royal Society| url=http://royalsociety.org/uploadedFiles/Royal_Society_Content/about-us/fellowship/Fellows_and_Foreign_Members.pdf|publisher=The Royal Society|access-date=2 May 2013}}</ref> and a Fellow of the American Mathematical Society in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2 May 2013|archive-date=25 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|url-status=dead}}</ref> She has served on the council of the Royal Society and in 2018 was its vice-president.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ulrike Tillmann |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/ulrike-tillmann-12419/ |access-date=14 March 2022 |website=royalsociety.org |publisher=Royal Society}}</ref> In 2017, she became a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/list-of-members/member/Member/show/ulrike-tillmann/|title=Ulrike Tillmann|publisher=[[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]]|access-date=5 January 2019}}</ref>

Tillmann was awarded the Bessel Prize by the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] in 2008<ref name="Isaac Newton Institute-2021">{{Cite web |date=4 February 2021 |title=Professor Ulrike Tillmann named as next Director of the Isaac Newton Institute |url=https://www.newton.ac.uk/news/ini-news/professor-ulrike-tillmann-named-as-next-director-of-the-isaac-newton-institute/ |access-date=14 March 2022 |website=Isaac Newton Institute |language=EN}}</ref> and was the [[Emmy Noether]] Lecturer of the [[German Mathematical Society]] in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mathematik.de/dmv/preise-auszeichnungen|title=Preise und Auszeichnungen|publisher=[[German Mathematical Society]]|language=de|access-date=5 November 2018}}</ref>

She was elected as president-designate of the London Mathematical Society in June 2020 and took over the presidency from [[Jonathan Keating]] in November 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=LMS President Designate Announced {{!}} London Mathematical Society|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news-entry/25062020-1347/lms-president-designate-announced|access-date=20 August 2020|website=www.lms.ac.uk}}</ref> She was elected to the {{ill|European Academy of Sciences|fr|Académie européenne des sciences}} (EURASC) in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=Member Profile – Prof. Ulrike Tillmann |url=https://www.eurasc.org/user/873/ulrike-tillmann |publisher=European Academy of Sciences |access-date=19 January 2022}}</ref> In October 2021 she became the director of the [[Isaac Newton Institute]], taking a post which lasts for five years.<ref name="Isaac Newton Institute-2021" />

== Personal life ==
Tillmann's parents are Ewald and Marie-Luise Tillmann. In 1995 she married Jonathan Morris with whom she has had three daughters.<ref name="ww" />

Tillmann is a member of the Oxford Jewish Congregation. As part of the celebration of the 750th anniversary of the founding of Merton College, she organized a symposium on the history of Merton College and its relationship with Oxford's Jewish community.<ref name="y229">{{cite web | title=Symbiosis through Time-Merton and its Jewish neighbours – Oxford Jewish Heritage | website=Oxford Jewish Heritage | date=2014-03-17 | url=https://www.oxfordjewishheritage.co.uk/symbiosis-through-time-merton-and-its-jewish-neighbours/ }}</ref>
